content: Flibanserin is indicated for premenopausal women diagnosed with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD). This condition is characterized by persistently low sexual desire that causes significant distress or interpersonal difficulties. The disorder must not be attributable to coexisting medical or psychiatric conditions, relationship problems, or the effects of medications or other substances. The recommended dose is 100 mg orally once daily at bedtime. Administration during waking hours is avoided due to increased risks of hypotension, syncope, accidental injury, and central nervous system (CNS) depression. If no improvement is observed after 8 weeks of treatment, discontinuation is advised. Acquired HSDD refers to a condition that develops in individuals who previously had no issues with sexual desire. Generalized HSDD occurs regardless of the type of stimulation, situation, or partner. Flibanserin is contraindicated with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as these drugs significantly increase flibanserin levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism. This interaction can lead to severe hypotension or syncope. Examples of such contraindicated drugs include: 1. Amiodarone 2. Aprepitant 3. Atazanavir 4. Bicalutamide 5. Ceritinib 6. Ciprofloxacin 7. Clarithromycin 8. Cobicistat 9. Conivaptan 10. Crizotinib 11. Cyclosporine 12. Darunavir 13. Diltiazem 14. Dronedarone 15. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF 16. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) 17. Ethanol: Co-administration with alcohol within 2 hours is contraindicated due to increased risk of severe hypotension and syncope. 18. Fluconazole 19. Fosamprenavir 20. Fosaprepitant 21. Grapefruit 22. Haloperidol 23. Idelalisib 24. Iloperidone 25. Imatinib 26. Indinavir 27. Isoniazid 28. Itraconazole 29. Ketoconazole 30. Lapatinib 31. Lenacapavir 32. Levo-ketoconazole 33. Lidocaine 34. Lopinavir 35. Metronidazole 36. Nefazodone 37. Nelfinavir 38. Netupitant/Palonosetron 39. Nicardipine 40. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: This combination is contraindicated with drugs highly dependent on CYP3A4 for clearance, as elevated concentrations can lead to serious or life-threatening reactions. 41. Posaconazole 42. Quinidine 43. Ritonavir 44. Schisandra 45. Sertraline 46. Tetracycline 47. Ticagrelor 48. Tipranavir 49. Verapamil The co-administration of flibanserin with any of the above substances is contraindicated due to the potential for severe adverse effects, including hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression.
